title: Cinemagraph
description: A cinemagraph is a still photograph in which one isolated element continues to move on a loop (steam, rain on glass, hair, a blink) while the rest of the frame is frozen. It is not a freeze-frame of a whole shot, and it is not a full clip that happens to loop.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The picture looks dead, then a kettle breathes. A coat is still.
Only the rain tracks the window. Time is allowed in one masked region.
The rest is a still. Use it when a photograph should refuse to fully stop: fashion, a poster that lives, a memory with one leak of motion.
The moving part must be plausible as a cycle. It is the wrong tool when the whole scene moves, or when all motion stops (freeze-frame).
If every element loops, that is an infinite loop of a shot, not a cinemagraph. If the loop is a boomerang of the entire take, that is a different toy.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Shoot a locked camera. Choose one motion that can cycle (steam, rain, flicker).
Mask that region in post, freeze the rest from a single frame, loop the live patch so the join is invisible. Prompt: almost a still, only one named element loops, locked camera, no other motion.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: A woman at a rain window, body frozen, only the rain and a thread of steam looping. Do not let her blink, the curtains blow, and the neon flicker all at once.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Freeze Frame stops everything. Infinite Loop repeats the entire shot.
Boomerang plays a whole action forward and back. A cinemagraph freezes the majority and loops a patch.
Time-Lapse advances the whole world in steps.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The form comes from fashion stills (Jamie Beck and Kevin Burg) and advertising, not from a single feature grammar. Fashion films and window displays are the well-known uses: one living detail in a still.
La Jetee is a cousin of stills and motion, not a cinemagraph loop.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: Wrong cousin: freeze-frame, full-shot loop, or a normal live take. Tell: several motions alive, a visible loop bump, or a frozen frame with no live patch.
Fix: one masked element, invisible join, everything else from a single still.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is a cinemagraph in film?
A still image with one isolated looping motion. The rest is frozen. It sits between a photograph and a clip.
Cinemagraph vs freeze-frame
A freeze-frame stops all motion. A cinemagraph stops almost all motion and keeps one element alive on a loop.
When should I use a cinemagraph?
When a still should have one living detail: steam, rain, a flicker. Do not use it if the whole scene needs to play, or if nothing should move.
How do I prompt a cinemagraph for AI image or video?
Say almost still, locked camera, and name the single looping element. Forbid additional motion and a visible loop cut.
